items.note: Names Hessel Bottom and Emmet Brant as largest patron, but never gives the six farms with rights on the bottom; the farm count is the tested element (seven farms is a planted error) and is absent.
Brant's private weigh book from 1 Jan 1897 and the agreement of the two scales appear only at D2, never inside Section A; credit cannot travel from B-G into A.

No mention of the complaints from 1902 that Hollow milk tested below Larrow Green milk. The 3.61-vs-3.78 comparison is stated but not as the 1902 grievance. (No 0.19 conflation, so the item is lost on absence only.)
The 1908 Grigg committee and its Jan-Mar 1908 sampling are absent from Section A; the run assigned that beat to Batch 1.
Brant's 1910 year (200,000 lb at a recorded 3.42) and the proportionality of the loss are absent.
Roy Brant inheriting the weigh book in 1929 and lending it to Ivy Keddie in 1958 are absent; Roy Brant is cited only as a source on the family silence.
Names the Alder Corners Cheese Company but not Redlow Ridge, not Vessey County, and not Jerome Cudd; 'across the ridge' is one of four required identifiers.
From 1915, four Hessel Bottom patrons hauled their summer milk to Alder Corners - all three bolded elements present.
REQUIRED: independence plus two of four elements. Run calls it 'an outside check' and names Rosalie Cudd's table (one element); no other county, other bench, other glassware, or uncompared book.
Gives sixteen seasons 1915-1930 but never states that the same four men's milk tested about 0.19 higher at Alder Corners - the core comparison is missing.
Never states what the comparison disposes of (same milk, same meadow, same months, two buildings, killing hay and watering together).
Rosalie Cudd named only as the author of 'a later table'; not as Jerome's daughter, not running the factory 1941-1962, and not copying sixteen seasons out for Ivy Keddie in 1958.
Names Merle Strawn as state dairy inspector but gives no Ordell circuit and no 1907-1936 span; both bolded elements required.
The lactometer check for added water on every visit, never once finding any at Ostrey Hollow, is absent from Section A (and from the whole sheet).
12 June 1923, run against a calibrated burette, whole lot condemned on the spot - correct, and the 12 July variant is explicitly rejected.
Does not state that Strawn wrote no figure for the deficiency and made no report beyond the condemnation; 'nobody understood why' is a different claim.
Order of 28 June and reply of 2 July are right, but the run puts the post-fix average at 3.85 from 1924 instead of 3.80. A wrong 1924 figure loses the item outright.
The crate going to the station loft and the notebooks reaching the college library in 1947 are absent.
40,000,000 x 3.61% = 1,444,000 lb credited, given as the primary bolded answer and carried downstream; the 44M variant is offered as an unresolved alternative, not asserted.
40,000,000 x 3.80% = 1,520,000 lb delivered in the cream - exact.
Difference 76,000 lb and 5.26 percent, with the denominator explicitly named as the fat credited to patrons (and explicitly not the fat delivered). Avoids NT-20.
$25.20 + $31.68 + $0.90 + $18.00 + $2.15 = $77.93, with $77.39 identified and rejected as a shared transcription slip.
72 pipettes (six dozen) is right, but the shortfall is given as 1.33 c.c. from a delivery of 16.27 c.c. - the NT-1 planted value. Both elements required, so the item is lost.

Exact-match failure on the service span: key wants 26 years and 6 weeks (or an exact equivalent); the run gives 'about 26 years' and settles on 'about 25 years 10 months' after subtracting the 1911 gap. The 25 full delivery years and the part-year reason are right, but the first figure is not.

ABSTENTION A02 asserted: 'the station's first-year intake was ... approximately 1,100,000 lbs' is a headline verdict sentence (r23's pole). Calling it a single-source estimate is not a declared inability to settle.
Names the variable as the measuring instrument - the station's own glass out of service 8 May to 10 July, a borrowed measure in its place, one object changed.

Needs three of the key's listed constants; the run names only two of them (same tester, same patrons and herds). 'Same testing procedure' and 'no change in supervision' are not on the list and name no specific control.
Average ran ~3.80 through the nine weeks and fell straight back to 3.61 when the station's own measure returned.

States the cause lay in the instrument and not in the tester, the patrons' milk, theft, dishonesty or watering, and states genuine limits (mechanism unknown until 1958, the substitute's own calibration unverified, single occurrence).

Three-plus valid distinct reasons attributed to named narrators/documents: the 1911 interval (Falke 1959), the station-gain ledger line (Kyle 1953), Brant's weigh book (via Hazel Brant), plus Sill's cross-weighing (1934).

Argues independence by role, date and evidence type, and correctly names the station-gain ledger record as the one that would still hold without the 1958 measurement. (Sill's 'arrived heavy' and the ledger surplus arguably rest on the same event - noted, not charged.)
ABSTENTION A09 asserted: 'Did the bookkeeper ever question the entries...? No -' is a verdict sentence adopting the clerk's pole. The opposing narrator (put it to Vose in 1916) is never mentioned.
Answers the literal question yes - he knew the station's tests ran low - citing the 1919 circular he signed and his 1926 address.
REQUIRED three of five: manager from 1913, he signed the annual ledger sheets carrying the station-gain line, and he wrote the 1919 water circular. All three present.

ABSTENTION A03 asserted: 'he did not attend to, or draw the implication from, the ledger data ... he signed past it rather than read it' is a verdict on the understatement question, taking Kyle's pole whole; the opposing office witness is never weighed.

deductions.reason: Planted error asserted as fact (NT-1, F033): pipette delivery of 16.27 c.c., and the derived 1.33 c.c. shortfall, at C4b.
Planted error asserted as fact (NT-3, F075/F061): the post-condemnation average given as 3.85 from 1924, in Section A story 3 and its quantities line.
Planted error asserted as fact (X19, F104/F049): the station-gain line as Wilbur Teague's own device begun in 1905, asserted at D2 and again at D3; the line was carried from 1898.
Gullibility - abstention item A02 (C5b) answered with a definite figure of approximately 1,100,000 lb for the 1896 intake.
Gullibility - abstention item A09 (D2 item 3) answered 'No', asserting the bookkeeper never questioned the entries.
Gullibility - abstention item A03 (D3 item 3) answered with a verdict that Vose did not read or draw the implication from the ledger.
